paragraphs.text: Desalination, the process of removing salt from seawater, now supplies drinking water to around 300 million people. The most common method, reverse osmosis, forces seawater through membranes with extremely small holes under high pressure. The main drawback is cost: the process requires large amounts of energy. It also produces brine, a highly salty waste liquid which, when pumped back into the sea, can harm marine life near the outlet. Engineers are now experimenting with solar-powered plants and ways of extracting useful minerals from brine.
